# Raised bed soil mix

## The beds

Three new beds built over Easter 2023 at the top end of plot 14 where the ground is all shillet and clay. Douglas fir boards from Bovey Timber, 2.4 m by 1.2 m, 30 cm deep (two 15 cm boards stacked). Corner posts 50 mm square. Boards cost £186 for the three beds, screws another £12.40. My grandson Alfie did the drilling, I did the measuring and the complaining.

Volume of each bed: 2.4 x 1.2 x 0.3 = 0.864 cubic metres. Call it 0.9 with settling. So about 2.6 cubic metres for all three, which is a lot more than it sounds when you see it on the drive.

## The recipe I settled on

After reading far too much, and ignoring most of it:

- 40% screened topsoil
- 40% green waste compost
- 20% sharp sand and 6 mm grit, half and half
- plus 2 handfuls of fish, blood and bone per square metre, raked into the top 10 cm

No peat. No vermiculite, too dear at the volume.

## Where it came from

### Topsoil

Ashburton Topsoils, one bulk bag of "premium screened", £78 delivered, ref order ATS-5520. It was decent but had couch grass roots in it. Spent two evenings picking those out.

### Compost

Green waste compost from the Dartmoor Recycling yard at £32 a bulk bag, collected in Colin Prowse's trailer. Smelled a bit sour on arrival; left it under a tarp for three weeks before using. Next time I'd mix in more of my own from the [[Compost pile]] but in 2023 I didn't have enough.

### Sand and grit

Six bags from Mole Valley Farmers, £5.25 each.

## Costs

All in all £339.65 for three beds, which went straight into the allotment column of my [[Budget spreadsheet]]. Without the boards it's about £50 a bed for the fill.

## How it behaved

### First season, 2023

Lovely. Carrots straight and long, no forking, which never happens in the clay. Beetroot fine. Lettuce bolted but that was the June heat, not the soil.

### Second season, 2024

The beds sank by 7 cm on average, worst in bed 2. Topped up in February 2024 with 50/50 home compost and the last of the topsoil. pH test (the little green Rapitest kit) read 6.4 in bed 1, 6.8 in bed 3. Bed 3 had a bit of lime from the brassicas the year before.

### Problems

- Bed 2 holds water at the far corner. Drilled two 10 mm holes in the bottom board, fixed it.
- Ants in bed 1 in August 2024. Kept it wetter and they moved on.
- Blackbirds flinging the mulch all over the path. Netting over in spring.

## What I'd change

Less grit, more compost. 30% grit was too sharp and dried out fast on the first try in 2023 (I started at 30/50/20 and changed to 40/40/20 after the first bed). For the garlic bed (see [[Garlic planting]]) I add an extra barrow of grit because it hates sitting wet over winter.

Clare asked what to use for her balcony in Valencia; I wrote it up for her in [[Huerto en el balcón]], though pots are another matter entirely.
